controls.label: Shape
controls.qualification: A sphere of the published radius, lit by Gar; the neutral gray is a display convention, not a measured color.
controls.notes: No image or color of GJ 486 b is published: the sphere has its measured size, and the gray marks an unresolved surface. The lighting is its own star's, at the measured orbit. The gray takes the color of gj-486's light, as its color dataset measures it.

charts.alt: The orbits of Gar's planets in this map from above, to scale, with GJ 486 b highlighted and the direction to Earth down. Each orbit is the one the app draws, from the published period, a/R*, eccentricity and argument of periastron; the star is a marker, not to scale.

GJ 486 b's transmission spectrum: the fraction of starlight the planet blocks as it crosses its star, larger where its atmosphere absorbs. 203 measured bins from Moran et al. 2023 (NASA 6.5m James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) Satellite Mission, Near Infrared Spectrograph (NIRSpec) - FIREFLy pipeline; NASA 6.5m James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) Satellite Mission, Near Infrared Spectrograph (NIRSpec) - Tiberius pipeline; NASA 6.5m James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) Satellite Mission, Near Infrared Spectrograph (NIRSpec) - Eureka! pipeline), as the NASA Exoplanet Archive lists them. Horizontal bars are wavelength bins; vertical bars are the published 1-sigma errors.

GJ 486 b crossing its star, as TESS recorded it: 2 sectors (23, 50) of the SPOC pipeline's 2-minute light curves of TIC 390651552, each transit divided by a straight line fitted to the light either side and folded onto the orbit the app draws, then averaged in 4-minute bins. Error bars are each bin's standard error.
